The project area contains approximately 5 miles of major streets and cross streets. It also contains approximately two and one-half miles of minor streets and alleyways. All streets observed within the project had sidewalks.
5. Project Neighborhoods
The project area is made up of a number of separate and distinct neighborhoods or subneighborhood areas. The areas may be more accurately described as subneighborhoods because they are segments of larger neighborhood areas that transverse or extend down into the project area. They are shown along with the Project Boundary Map, appendix C of this report.
The delineation of Neighborhood Areas is often based on a number of different factors - - social or ethnic make-up, land use pattern, geographic barriers, income levels, age characteristics, etc. In this case, three main factors existed in the delineation of those neighborhoods observed in the project area. These factors are (1) hand use, (2) age characteristics, (3) income levels. The project neighborhoods are discussed as follows:
a. Neighborhood #1:
This neighborhood extends through the project and is identified by its predominant land use characteristics -- professional/business. Although there are some buildings specifically built for office space, the majority of the structures housing professional people and businesses are converted single family or multifamily residential structures, most of which are located along Front Street. This area is zoned for both residential and nonresidential land use, with the exception of the homes along the eastern side of 2nd Street and a few at the south end of the project along Front Street. Most of the neighborhood land use has been converted to nonresidential office space, e.g., doctors, dentists, professional organizations, insurance companies.
Other than the threat of damage from flooding, this is a very desirable area for businesses and professional people to locate. It is an old, well-known area that is close to downtown (CBD). The property along Front Street provides an excellent view of the River and within this area the Governor's Mansion for the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania is located. The Major arterial streets in this neighborhood; Front Street, one way south, and Second Street, one way north form State/Federal Routes 22 and 322. Macley Street within the project area is also included in the highway system; it is a two way street. Traffic in this area is discussed later in the section covering the aspects of noise from passing vehicles on Front Street.
